passages.text: The following discussion analyzes our financial condition and results of operations and should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, wherein WES Operating is fully consolidated, and which are included under Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K, and the information set forth in Risk Factors under Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K. Discussion of 2023 items, and comparison of the year ended December 31, 2024, to the year ended December 31, 2023, that are not included in this annual report on Form 10-K can be found under Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, which is included under Part II, Item 7 of our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, as filed with the SEC on February 26, 2025, and is available via the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov and our website at www.westernmidstream.com. The Partnership’s assets include assets owned and ownership interests accounted for by us under the equity method of accounting, through our 98.1% partnership interest in WES Operating, as of December 31, 2025. Amounts attributable to noncontrolling interests presented in this Item 7 consist of (i) the 25% third-party interest in Chipeta for all periods presented, and only for natural-gas assets for throughput attributable to WES, and (ii) the 1.9%, 2.0%, and 2.0% limited partner interest in WES Operating as of December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, owned by an Occidental subsidiary. See Note 1—Summary of Significant Accounting Policies and Basis of Presentation and Note 7—Equity Investments in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements under Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K. We also own and control the entire non-economic general partner interest in WES Operating GP, and our general partner is owned by Occidental. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY We are a midstream energy company organized as a publicly traded partnership, engaged in the business of gathering, compressing, treating, processing, and transporting natural gas; gathering, stabilizing, and transporting condensate, NGLs, and crude oil; and gathering, transporting, recycling, treating, supplying, and disposing of produced water. In our capacity as a natural - gas processor, we also buy and sell residue, NGLs, and condensate on behalf of ourselves and our customers under certain contracts. To provide superior midstream service, we focus on ensuring the reliability and performance of our systems, creating sustainable cost efficiencies, enhancing our safety culture, and protecting the environment. We own or have investments in assets located in Texas, New Mexico, and the Rocky Mountains (Colorado, Utah, and Wyoming). While a 10% change in the applicable benchmark interest rate would not materially impact interest expense on our outstanding borrowings at December 31, 2025, it would impact the fair value of the senior notes. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow covers gross interest expense by a comfortable margin, and the coverage ratio sits well above the sector median, indicating the midstream asset base generates stable fee-based cash flows that comfortably service fixed charges through the cycle.

Operating margin is materially higher than the sector median, reflecting the partnership's integrated gathering, processing and treating footprint across the Permian and Rocky Mountains, which supports pricing power and cost absorption relative to natural gas transmission peers.

key_risks.text: The debt note shows a large senior note maturity due in the near term, and the partnership has historically relied on refinancing and revolver capacity to manage maturities. A refinancing at higher rates would lift interest expense and pressure coverage, particularly if benchmark rates rise.

Leverage sits above the indicative upgrade threshold and the partnership's cash distributions to unitholders absorb most operating cash flow, leaving limited retained cash for debt reduction. This constrains the pace of deleveraging and keeps the financial risk profile in the significant tier.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating income covers gross interest expense at a level above the sector median, and operating cash flow is sufficient to fund distributions and modest capital spending. However, the absence of a capex tag prevents a precise free cash flow calculation, which is material to assessing true debt-servicing headroom.

The current ratio exceeds the sector median, indicating adequate near-term liquidity, and cash balances provide a modest buffer against net debt. Still, the partnership's debt is almost entirely fixed-rate senior notes, so refinancing risk rather than floating-rate exposure is the primary servicing consideration.

overall_credit_view.text: The partnership's leverage is well below the sector median and coverage is above median, but the indicative financial risk profile remains significant because cash flow to debt sits in a middle tier. Deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth or debt reduction, both of which face headwinds from distributions.

Our forward view is that credit quality is stable but constrained by the partnership's distribution policy and refinancing needs. A sustained reduction in leverage or improved cash flow retention would be required to move toward a stronger profile, while a material debt-funded acquisition or EBITDA decline could pressure the current standing.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流以舒適的幅度覆蓋總利息支出，且覆蓋率遠高於行業中位數，顯示中游資產基礎產生穩定的收費型現金流，足以在週期內輕鬆償付固定費用。
營運利潤率顯著高於行業中位數，反映該合夥企業在二疊紀盆地及洛磯山脈地區一體化的集輸、加工和處理佈局，這支撐了相對於天然氣輸送同業的定價能力和成本吸收能力。

key_risks.text: 債務說明顯示近期有一筆大額優先票據到期，而該合夥企業歷來依賴再融資和循環信貸額度來管理到期債務。以更高利率進行再融資將推高利息支出並對覆蓋率構成壓力，尤其是在基準利率上升的情況下。
槓桿率高於指示性上調門檻，且該合夥企業向單位持有人的現金分派吸收了大部分營運現金流，留存的現金有限，難以用於削減債務。這制約了去槓桿的速度，並使財務風險狀況維持在顯著級別。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運利潤覆蓋總利息支出的水平高於行業中位數，且營運現金流足以支付分派和適度的資本支出。然而，缺乏資本支出標籤導致無法精確計算自由現金流，而這對評估真實的償債空間至關重要。
流動比率超過行業中位數，顯示短期流動性充足，且現金餘額為淨債務提供了適度的緩衝。儘管如此，該合夥企業的債務幾乎全部為固定利率優先票據，因此再融資風險而非浮動利率風險是主要的償債考量因素。

overall_credit_view.text: 該合夥企業的槓桿率遠低於行業中位數，且覆蓋率高於中位數，但指示性財務風險狀況仍為顯著，因為現金流對債務的比率處於中間層級。去槓桿取決於EBITDA增長或債務削減，而兩者都面臨來自分派的阻力。
我們的前瞻觀點是，信用質量穩定，但受該合夥企業的分派政策和再融資需求所制約。要邁向更強勁的狀況，需要持續降低槓桿或改善現金流留存，而重大債務融資收購或EBITDA下降則可能對當前狀況構成壓力。
